acquisitions.description: 19 urgent care centers including HeadFirst sports injury and concussion clinics; approximately 300 employees
Pediatric evidence-based incentive program integrated into MedStar clinical operations

legalIssues.description: Unauthorized access to three employee email accounts between January and October 2023, affecting 183,000+ individuals. Settled for $1.35 million. Final approval November 2025.
DOJ sued MedStar for denying hospital access to non-patient support persons for people with disabilities during COVID-19. Consent decree approved February 5, 2024; $440,000 settlement.
St. Mary's County jury awarded $1.5 million against MedStar St. Mary's Hospital for surgeon leaving part of gallbladder behind during surgery.
Class action filed seeking $5M+ in damages after MedStar suspended physician over patient concerns about behavior.

ratios.investmentsToOperatingIncomeInterpretati: MedStar's $2.66B investment portfolio is 16.7x its $159M operating income, indicating massive balance sheet wealth relative to thin operating margins typical of a system claiming nonprofit status.

ratios.charityCareVsStateInterpretation: Maryland state average is 6.6% of operating expenses (FY2023). MedStar system-wide percentage not separately verified.

accusation: MedStar Health holds a $2.66 billion investment portfolio — 16.7 times its $159 million operating income — while paying its CEO $7.2 million in total compensation, carrying $1.63 billion in tax-exempt bond debt, closing pediatric and postpartum units, and laying off hundreds of workers, all under the shelter of tax-exempt nonprofit status as the Baltimore Ravens' official medical partner.
